title: Geometric-mean inequalities for generalized sine and hyperbolic sine
statement:
For $p,q>1$, define the generalized sine functions ${\rm sin}_{p,q}$ and ${\rm sinh}_{p,q}$ as the inverses of ${\rm arcsin}_{p,q}$ and ${\rm arsinh}_{p,q}$, respectively, and let $r,s\in(0,1)$. **Geometric-mean conjecture.**

$$
{\rm sin}_{p,q}(\sqrt{r s})\leq\sqrt{{\rm sin}_{p,q}(r){\rm sin}_{p,q}(s)}.
$$

$$
{\rm sinh}_{p,q}(\sqrt{r s})\geq\sqrt{{\rm sinh}_{p,q}(r){\rm sinh}_{p,q}(s)}.
$$

These inequalities would extend analogous geometric-mean inequalities for the classical hyperbolic functions to the generalized trigonometric setting. The source presents them on the basis of computer experiments and does not report a proof or resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.0483

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2011).
source_name: Barkat Ali Bhayo and Matti Vuorinen, “On generalized trigonometric functions with two parameters”, arXiv:1112.0483 (2012).
